title: A Curriculum Learning-Based Adaptive Trajectory Tracking Approach for Omni-Drive Robots in Dynamic Environments
content: Trajectory tracking for holonomic drive systems remains a significant challenge, particularly in complex and dynamic environments. This demands the development of effective control algorithms capable of following pre-defined trajectories while simultaneously avoiding obstacles. In this work, we propose a model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach integrated with curriculum learning for omni-directional mobile robots. We design a specialized RL architecture that leverages only the most relevant inputs, such as trajectory error and relative obstacle positions, to enable efficient and safe path planning. The control policies are trained in a simulated environment using a diverse trajectory patterns and external disturbances. Curriculum learning is applied hierarchically, gradually increasing environmental complexity to enhance both learning efficiency and generalization capability. The performance of the tracking model is quantitatively evaluated using the success rate and mean tracking error. Simulation results demonstrate a 90 percent success rate across 100 randomized tracking tasks in previously unseen complex scenarios. Furthermore, the proposed DRL controller with curriculum learning exhibits improved stability, faster training convergence, and robust disturbance rejection capabilities compared to learning from scratch.
